haemet_he_meteg.source_evidence: In human-80b.png, which is a crop and enlargement of source item 80 on s174 row 5, word 25 הָאֱמֶת shows two separate marks under the initial he. The qamatz is the T-shaped mark under the right half of the he. To its left, still within the he's width, is a separate short vertical stroke. That stroke stands clear of the qamatz, and it lies to the right of the alef's hataf-segol cluster (three dots plus a colon pair), so it belongs to the he and not the alef. It has the same shape as the vertical stroke under the tsade of וָצֶֽדֶק in the same crop. It is also not the tipcha: the tipcha is the separate curved stroke under the mem beside the segol. The same qamatz-plus-vertical-stroke pair can be seen at smaller size in human-80.png and s174-row5.png. I decided this from the print alone, not from grammar or from parallel words like הָֽעוֹלָם. The human did not answer this question: the human's answer for 80 covered only the mem tipcha.
